source.title: Towards an Understanding of Benign Overfitting in Neural Networks
source.authors: Zhu Li; Zhi-Hua Zhou; A. Gretton

record.file_problem: none; the full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The paper develops finite-sample theory for a two-layer ReLU network interpolator and refines the double-descent account: its results predict risk growth beyond O(n²) parameters and say multiple descent is possible with covariate noise. It does not report a full empirical size sweep.
record.gate_note: The paper reports theoretical bounds and explicit theoretical predictions, not numerical measurements from an empirical sweep. Empirical results cited from other work are not recorded as rows.
record.test_reason: Finite-sample theory for a minimum-norm two-layer ReLU random-feature interpolator (first layer fixed), with noisy covariates and d=O(n^α). Its variance lower bound grows like s/(nd) past interpolation, and the authors predict risk rises again once s=Ω(n²). That is a specific theoretical result that the second descent of V4 does not continue indefinitely in this model. No empirical sweep is reported.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that the two-layer ReLU MNLS interpolator's excess risk can vanish, with a near minimax O(sqrt(log n/n)) rate under conditions on α, γ, ζ. They predict risk increases once s exceeds O(n²), which they call a generalization of double descent. Multiple descent with covariate noise is claimed as possible and matched to cited empirical work, not derived as an explicit curve.
record.recipe_differences: Finite-sample theoretical analysis of a minimum-norm two-layer ReLU interpolator, with fixed first-layer weights and covariate noise; no empirical size-sweep recipe is reported.
record.method_sensitivity: The risk bounds depend on dimension growth α, covariance spectrum decay γ, covariate-noise decay ζ, and parameter count s. The paper states that bias convergence depends on these conditions and that poor noise decay can make bias diverge.

fits_no_version.finding: Covariate noise acts as implicit regularization that enables benign overfitting. The authors say adding noise can improve generalization.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Noise in the input covariates acts as implicit regularization that makes interpolating networks generalize.

record.problems: The paper provides theoretical bounds rather than a direct empirical sweep of the risk curve. Its analysis assumes subgaussian data and covariate noise, and applies to d < n; the authors state these limitations.
record.rows_left_out: No relevant reported outcomes over the 60-row limit.

untested.parts: All of it. There is no trained deep network, no size sweep, and no peak near the interpolation threshold; only s>n>d is analysed.
The under-parameterized side, the peak at interpolation, an actual second descent, and model classes other than two-layer ReLU random features.
Label-noise dependence, observed multiple peaks, and removal of the peak by optimally tuned regularization.
Not studied (n is not swept near a threshold).

missing.what: Bias upper bound BR ≤ c(sqrt(s/n·log(1/δ)) + d²σξ/n), with its convergence conditions and divergence when α, ζ are near 1
Combined excess-risk bound O(sqrt(s/n·log s)+d²σξ/n+s/(nd)); example rates O(n^-0.25) at s=O(n^1.25) and near minimax O(sqrt(log n/n)) at s/n constant

record.verdict_notes: The 'network' has a fixed random first layer (random-feature regression), so V1 links were removed. The record's 'supports' label for V6 is dropped: the bounds cannot show several peaks. All results are theoretical bounds up to universal constants, so the s-dependence is only up to order.

versions.untested_parts: The paper does not test a full fall-rise-fall curve or locate a peak near the size that just fits the training data; it analyzes only the overparameterized regime s > n > d.
No risk sweep over training epochs or training time.
No sweep over the number of training samples near an interpolation threshold.
The analysis is for a two-layer ReLU network, not a range of model classes, and does not establish the full curve across capacities.
The paper does not test whether one effective-complexity measure predicts peak locations across axes.
The paper does not test label-noise dependence, multiple observed peak locations, or whether optimally tuned regularization removes a peak.
The paper does not recount complexity using an effective number of parameters or test whether that makes the curve U-shaped.

rows.subject: MNLS estimator for one-hidden-layer ReLU neural network
rows.stage_stated: Minimum-norm interpolator; first-layer weights are kept constant
rows.operation_detail: Theoretical upper bound on variance as parameter count s varies

conditions.value: independent subgaussian noise; σξ² = O(d^-ζ), ζ ≥ 1
λi ∝ i^-γ, γ > 1; Theorem 1 also requires its stated k* condition

rows.uncertainty: With probability 1 − 4e^(-d/c) − 4e^(-s/c); c > 1 is a universal constant
rows.note: An upper bound proportional to s in the stated overparameterized regime; this does not establish the complete test-risk curve.
rows.check: The model is a two-layer network with a fixed random first layer and only the output layer fit (closed-form MNLS), not a trained deep network, so V1 does not apply. An upper bound on variance that grows linearly in s cannot show whether risk improves with capacity.

rows.subject: MNLS estimator for one-hidden-layer ReLU neural network
rows.stage_stated: Minimum-norm interpolator; first-layer weights are kept constant
rows.operation_detail: Theoretical lower bound on variance as parameter count s varies

conditions.value: independent subgaussian noise; σξ² = O(d^-ζ), ζ ≥ 1

rows.uncertainty: With probability greater than 1 − 5e^(-d/c) − 2e^(-s/c); c > 1 is a universal constant
rows.note: Together with the upper bound, this gives variance of order s/(nd) in the stated regime; it is not a complete test-risk curve.
rows.check: V1 removed (random-feature model, no peak region analysed). The lower bound VR ≥ (1/c)σ0² Tr(Σ) s/(nd) grows with s for s>n, the opposite of risk improving with capacity. Since MR=0 is assumed, risk is at least the variance.

rows.value: The bounds indicate that multiple descent, rather than double descent, is possible in the presence of covariate noise
